questions.question: A random variable X has probability density function f(x) as given below: [latex]f(x)=\left\{\begin{matrix} a+bx & for \; 0 \lt x \lt 1\\ 0& otherwise \end{matrix}\right.[/latex] If the expected value E[X]=2/3, then [latex]Pr[X \lt 0.5][/latex] is _____________.
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} f(x)&=\left\{\begin{matrix} a+bx & \text{for }0 \lt x \lt 1\\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{matrix}\right.&\\ \text{Now given }E(X)&=2/3\\ \int_{0}^{1}xf(x)dx&=\frac{2}{3}\\ \int_{0}^{1}x(a+bx)dx&=\frac{2}{3}\\ a\left ( \frac{x^2}{2} \right )_0^1+b\left ( \frac{x^3}{3} \right )_0^1&=\frac{2}{3}\\ a\left ( \frac{1}{2} \right )+b\left ( \frac{1}{3} \right )&=\frac{2}{3}\\ 3a+2b&=4\;\;...(i)\\ \text{Now, }\int_{0}^{1}f(x)dx &=1\\ (\text{total probability} & \text{ is always equal to 1})\\ \int_{0}^{1}(a+bx)dx&=\left ( ax+\frac{bx^2}{2} \right )_0^1=1\\ a+\frac{b}{2}&=1\\ 2a+b&=2\;\;...(ii)\\ \text{Now solving } & \text{ (i) and (ii), we get}\\ a&=0,b=2\\ So,\; \;f(x)&=\left\{\begin{matrix} 2x & \text{for }0 \lt x lt 1\\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{matrix}\right.&\\ \text{Now we need}&\\ P(x \lt 0.5)&=\int_{0}^{0.5}2xdx=2\left ( \frac{x^2}{2} \right )_0^{0.5}\\ &=0.5^2-0^2=0.25 \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} C_1&=0.01P_1^2+30P_1+10\\ \frac{dC_1}{dP_1}&=2 \times 0.01P_1+30\\ &=0.02P_1+30\\ C_2&=0.05P_2^2+10P_2+10\\ \frac{dC-2}{dP_2}&=0.1P_2+10\\ \text{For optimum } &\text{incremental cost,}\\ \frac{dC_1}{dP_1}&=\frac{dC_2}{dP_2}\\ 0.02P_1+30&=0.1P_2+10\\ 0.02P_1-0.1P_2&=-20 \;\;...(i)\\ \text{Given, }P_1+P_2&=200 \;\;...(ii)\\ \text{Solving } & \text{equation (i) and (ii),}\\ P_2&=200, P_1=0\\ \text{But the }& \text{range of }P_1 \text{ and }P_2 \text{ are specified as}\\ 100MW \leq & P_1 \leq 150MW\\ 100MW \leq & P_2 \leq 180MW\\ \text{hence, }& P_2=200 MW \text{ is not valid}\\ \text{so, both }& P_1 \text{ and } P_2 \text{ are operating at}\\ P_1=100,P_2=100\;& \Rightarrow \; P_1+P_2=200\\ IC_1=\frac{dC_1}{dP_1}&=0.02 \times P_1+30=32 Rs/MW\\ IC_2=\frac{dC_2}{dP_2}&=0.1 \times P_2+10=20 Rs/MW \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: A 50 Hz generating unit has H-constant of 2 MJ/MVA. The machine is initially operating in steady state at synchronous speed, and producing 1 pu of real power. The initial value of the rotor angle [latex]\delta[/latex] is 5[latex]^{\circ}[/latex], when a bolted three phase to ground short circuit fault occurs at the terminal of the generator. Assuming the input mechanical power to remain at 1 pu, the value of [latex]\delta[/latex] in degrees, 0.02 second after the fault is _________.
questions.explanation:
Let [latex]3-\phi[/latex] fault occurs at t=0 [latex]\Rightarrow \; P_e=0\text{ for }t\geq 0^+[/latex] Now, swing equation for [latex]t\geq 0^+[/latex] [latex]\begin{aligned}
\frac{2H}{\omega _s}\frac{d^2\delta }{dt^2} &=P_m \\ 
 \frac{d^2\delta }{dt^2}&= \frac{P_m \omega _s }{2H}\\ 
\frac{d\delta }{dt}&= \frac{P_m \omega _s }{2H}t+C\\ 
 C=\left.\begin{matrix}
\frac{d\delta }{dt}
\end{matrix}\right| _{t=0^+}&=\omega (t=0^+)-\omega _s\\ 
 C=\omega _s-\omega _s&=0\;(\omega (t-0^+)=\omega _s) \\ 
 \frac{d\delta }{dt}&=\frac{P_m \omega _s }{2H}t \\ 
 \Rightarrow \; \delta &= \frac{P_m \omega _s }{4H}t^2+C'\\ 
 C'&= \delta |_{t=0^+}=\delta _0\\ 
\delta  &= \frac{P_m \omega _s }{4H}t^2+\delta _0\\
\text{Now in problem,}\\
\delta (t=0.02)&\\
&=\frac{1 \times 2  \times 180  \times 50 \times 0.02^2 +5^{\circ}}{4 \times 2}\\
&=5.9^{\circ}
\end{aligned}[/latex]

So, [latex]I(0^+)=0[/latex] The KVL in th loop will be [latex]V=RI+L\frac{dI}{dt}[/latex] At [latex]t=0^+ [/latex] [latex]V=RI(0^+)+L\frac{dI}{dt}(0^+) [/latex] Since, [latex] I(0^+)=0 [/latex] So, [latex]\frac{dI}{dt}(0^+)=\frac{V}{L} [/latex] Now, lets differentiate the above equation So,[latex] \frac{dV}{dt}=R\frac{dI}{dt}+L\frac{d^2I}{dt^2} [/latex] [latex]\;\;0=R\frac{dI}{dt}+L\frac{d^2I}{dt^2} [/latex] At [latex]t=0^+[/latex] [latex] 0=R\frac{dI}{dt}(0^+)+L\frac{d^2I}{dt^2}(0^+) [/latex] So, [latex] \frac{d^2I}{dt^2}(0^+)=-\frac{R}{L^2}\cdot V[/latex]

Initially [latex](t=0^-)[/latex] the inductor would be uncharged.
So, [latex]I(0^+)=0[/latex]
The KVL in th loop will be
[latex]V=RI+L\frac{dI}{dt}[/latex]
At [latex]t=0^+ [/latex]
[latex]V=RI(0^+)+L\frac{dI}{dt}(0^+) [/latex]
Since, [latex] I(0^+)=0 [/latex]

[latex]\;\;0=R\frac{dI}{dt}+L\frac{d^2I}{dt^2} [/latex]
At [latex]t=0^+[/latex]
[latex] 0=R\frac{dI}{dt}(0^+)+L\frac{d^2I}{dt^2}(0^+) [/latex]
So, [latex] \frac{d^2I}{dt^2}(0^+)=-\frac{R}{L^2}\cdot V[/latex]

questions.question: The unit step response of a system with the transfer function [latex]G(s)=\frac{1-2s}{1+s}[/latex] is given by which one of the following waveforms?
questions.explanation: [latex]T.F.=\frac{1-2s}{1+s} [/latex] [latex]C(s)=\frac{1-2s}{1+s}\cdot \frac{1}{s} [/latex] [latex]\;\;=\frac{A}{1+s}+\frac{B}{s} [/latex] For A, [latex]A=\lim_{s \to -1}(s+1)\cdot \frac{1-2s}{s(1+s)} [/latex] [latex]\;\;=\frac{(1-2(-1))}{(-1)}=-3 [/latex] For B, [latex]B=\lim_{s \to 0}s\cdot \frac{1-2s}{s(1+s)}=1 [/latex] [latex]C(s)=\frac{1}{s}-\frac{3}{1+s} [/latex] [latex]C(t)=(1-3e^{-t})u(t)[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
[latex]T.F.=\frac{1-2s}{1+s} [/latex]
[latex]C(s)=\frac{1-2s}{1+s}\cdot \frac{1}{s} [/latex]
[latex]\;\;=\frac{A}{1+s}+\frac{B}{s} [/latex]
For A,
[latex]A=\lim_{s \to -1}(s+1)\cdot \frac{1-2s}{s(1+s)} [/latex]
[latex]\;\;=\frac{(1-2(-1))}{(-1)}=-3 [/latex]
For B,
[latex]B=\lim_{s \to 0}s\cdot \frac{1-2s}{s(1+s)}=1 [/latex]
[latex]C(s)=\frac{1}{s}-\frac{3}{1+s} [/latex]
[latex]C(t)=(1-3e^{-t})u(t)[/latex]

questions.question: An open loop transfer function G(s) of a system is [latex]G(s)=\frac{K}{s(s+1)(s+2)}[/latex] For a unity feedback system, the breakaway point of the root loci on the real axis occurs at,
questions.explanation: [latex]G_1(s)=\frac{k}{s(s+1)(s+2)} [/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \;\; 1+\frac{k}{s(s+1)(s+2)}=0 [/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \;\; s(s^2+3s+2)+k=0 [/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \;\; s^3+3s^2+2s+k=0 [/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \;\; k=-s^3-3s^2-2s\;\;\;...(i) [/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \;\;\frac{dk}{ds}=0[/latex] [latex] \;\;\;\;\frac{dk}{ds}=-3s^2-6s-2=0[/latex] [latex] \;\;\;\;s=-0.422,-1.577[/latex] Only s=-0.422 lie on root locus. Therefore brakaway point is s=-0.42.
questions.explanation_html:
[latex]G_1(s)=\frac{k}{s(s+1)(s+2)} [/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \;\; 1+\frac{k}{s(s+1)(s+2)}=0 [/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \;\; s(s^2+3s+2)+k=0 [/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \;\; s^3+3s^2+2s+k=0 [/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \;\; k=-s^3-3s^2-2s\;\;\;...(i) [/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \;\;\frac{dk}{ds}=0[/latex]
[latex] \;\;\;\;\frac{dk}{ds}=-3s^2-6s-2=0[/latex]
[latex] \;\;\;\;s=-0.422,-1.577[/latex]

Only s=-0.422 lie on root locus. Therefore brakaway point is s=-0.42.

questions.question: For the system governed by the set of equations: [latex]dx_{1}/dt=2x_{1}+x_{2}+u [/latex] [latex]dx_{2}/dt=-2x_{1}+u [/latex] [latex] y=3x_{1}[/latex] the transfer function Y(s)/U(s) is given by
questions.explanation: [latex]\frac{dx_1}{dt}=2x_1+x_2+u\;\;\;...(i) [/latex] [latex]\frac{dx_2}{dt}=-2x_1+4\;\;\;\;...(ii)[/latex] From equation (i), [latex]sx_1=2x_1+x_2+u [/latex] [latex]sx_2=-2x_1+u [/latex] [latex]x_2=\left ( -\frac{2x_1+u}{s} \right ) [/latex] [latex]sx_1=2x_1+\left ( -\frac{2x_1+u}{s} \right )+4 [/latex] [latex]sx_1-2x_1+\frac{2x_1}{s}=\frac{4}{5}+4 [/latex] [latex]x_1\left ( s-2+\frac{2}{s} \right )=u\left (1+\frac{1}{s} \right ) [/latex] [latex]\frac{x_1}{4}=\frac{\left ( 1+\frac{1}{s} \right )}{\left ( s-2+\frac{2}{s} \right )} [/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \;\;\frac{y}{u}=\frac{3x-1}{u}=\frac{3\left ( 1+\frac{1}{s} \right )}{\left ( s-2+\frac{2}{s} \right )} [/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \;\;\frac{y}{u}=\frac{3(s+1)}{(s^2-2s+2)}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
[latex]\frac{dx_1}{dt}=2x_1+x_2+u\;\;\;...(i) [/latex]
[latex]\frac{dx_2}{dt}=-2x_1+4\;\;\;\;...(ii)[/latex]
From equation (i),
[latex]sx_1=2x_1+x_2+u [/latex]
[latex]sx_2=-2x_1+u [/latex]
[latex]x_2=\left ( -\frac{2x_1+u}{s} \right ) [/latex]
[latex]sx_1=2x_1+\left ( -\frac{2x_1+u}{s} \right )+4 [/latex]
[latex]sx_1-2x_1+\frac{2x_1}{s}=\frac{4}{5}+4 [/latex]
[latex]x_1\left ( s-2+\frac{2}{s} \right )=u\left (1+\frac{1}{s} \right ) [/latex]
[latex]\frac{x_1}{4}=\frac{\left ( 1+\frac{1}{s} \right )}{\left ( s-2+\frac{2}{s} \right )} [/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \;\;\frac{y}{u}=\frac{3x-1}{u}=\frac{3\left ( 1+\frac{1}{s} \right )}{\left ( s-2+\frac{2}{s} \right )} [/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \;\;\frac{y}{u}=\frac{3(s+1)}{(s^2-2s+2)}[/latex]
